facts.statement: Aplestosuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 93.5 to 83.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating probably to the Turonian or the Santonian stage of the late Cretaceous, about 93.5-83.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Aplestosuchus were discovered in the Buruti creek area of the General Salgado municipality in southern Brazil.
facts.quote: LPRP/USP 0229 was found in the Buruti creek area, of the General Salgado municipality, São Paulo, in southern Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus name Aplestosuchus combines the Greek word for "insatiate" or "gluttonous" with the name of the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Greek aplestos, meaning "insatiate", "gluttonous", and suchus, Latinized from the Greek souchos, an Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.

facts.statement: The species name sordidus means "filthy" and refers to the animal's greedy predatory behavior.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from the Latin sordidus, meaning "filthy", in reference to the greedy behavior of the animal, demonstrated by the predation of another closely related crocodyliform, an unidentified sphagesaurid.

facts.statement: The single known specimen of Aplestosuchus measures more than one meter from the tip of the skull to the base of the tail.
facts.quote: The only known specimen of Aplestosuchus is more than one meter long from the tip of the skull to the base of the tail.

facts.statement: Aplestosuchus was a fully terrestrial predator, similar to other baurusuchids.
facts.quote: Aplestosuchus, like other baurusuchids, was a fully terrestrial predator.

facts.statement: The skeleton of Aplestosuchus sordidus preserves the remains of an unidentified sphagesaurid crocodyliform inside its abdominal cavity.
facts.quote: A. sordidus is represented by a single articulated and nearly complete skeleton, preserving the remains of an unidentified sphagesaurid crocodyliform in its abdominal cavity.

facts.statement: The discovery of a crocodyliform inside Aplestosuchus provides direct fossil evidence of predation between different crocodyliform taxa.
facts.quote: The find represents direct evidence of predation between different taxa of crocodyliforms in the fossil record.

facts.statement: Aplestosuchus is distinguished by unique skull features, including a nasal bone with a dorsal midline crest and a frontal ridge reaching the midline between the prefrontals.
facts.quote: It possesses an autapomorphic nasal bone with dorsal midline crest, and an autapomorphic frontal longitudinal ridge that reaches the midline contact between the prefrontals.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Aplestosuchus has outer sculpture limited to the dentary bone and lacks a peg on the occipital surface of the mandibular symphysis.
facts.quote: In the lower jaw of Aplestosuchus, the outer sculpture of the mandible is limited to the dentary, and the occipital surface of the mandibular symphysis lack a peg.

facts.statement: Aplestosuchus is classified within the family Baurusuchidae, alongside other genera like Campinasuchus and Gondwanasuchus.
facts.quote: Aplestosuchus, along with the recently described baurusuchids Campinasuchus and Gondwanasuchus, were scored into the taxon-character matrix of Montefeltro et al. (2011), which is focused solely on Baurusuchidae

facts.statement: Aplestosuchus belongs to the family Baurusuchidae.
facts.quote: familia: Baurusuchidae

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Aplestosuchus measures over one meter in length from the skull tip to the base of the tail.
facts.quote: El espécimen de Aplestosuchus mide más de un metro de largo desde la punta del cráneo hasta la base de la cola.

facts.statement: Aplestosuchus was a fully terrestrial predator, like other baurusuchids.
facts.quote: Aplestosuchus, como otros baurusúquidos, era un depredador completamente terrestre.

facts.statement: Baurusuchids, which could reach over four meters in length, were among the super-predators of Late Cretaceous South American ecosystems.
facts.quote: Alcanzando más de cuatro metros de longitud, los baurusúquidos estaban entre los superdepredadores de los ecosistemas del Cretácico Superior de Suramérica.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that sphagesaurid material found in the abdominal cavity of Aplestosuchus resulted from active predation rather than scavenging.
facts.quote: Se considera que el material de esfagesáurido recuperado en la cavidad abdominal de Aplestosuchus se debe a la depredación y no al consumo de carroña

facts.statement: Aplestosuchus is distinguished from all other known crocodiliforms by a unique combination of traits, including four autapomorphies.
facts.quote: Aplestosuchus se distingue de todos los otros crocodiliformes conocidos por una combinación única de rasgos, incluyendo cuatro autapomorfias.

facts.statement: Aplestosuchus possesses an autapomorphic nasal bone with a mid-dorsal crest and a longitudinal frontal crest reaching the mid-contact between the prefrontals.
facts.quote: Posee un hueso nasal autapomórfico con una cresta dorsal en el medio, y una cresta frontal longitudinal que alcanza el contacto medio entre los prefrontales.

facts.statement: The medial supratemporal border of Aplestosuchus is crest-shaped, and the border along the ectopterygoid-yugal suture has a notch in its posterior part.
facts.quote: Su borde medial supratemporal tiene forma de cresta, y el borde a lo largo de la sutura entre el ectopterigoide y el yugal tien una muesca en su parte caudal.

facts.statement: A lateral depression is present on the quadrate bone of Aplestosuchus.
facts.quote: Una depresión lateral se encuentra en su hueso cuadrado.

facts.statement: The palatine bone bar in Aplestosuchus is crested on its ventral surface but cylindrical on its dorsal part.
facts.quote: La barra del hueso palatino es crestada en su superficie ventral, mientras que es cílindrica en su parte dorsal.

facts.statement: The coanal septum in Aplestosuchus is also crested on its ventral surface.
facts.quote: El septo coanal también es crestado en su superficie ventral.

facts.statement: A single rostrolateral paracoanal fossa leading to the paracoanal fenestra is located at the base of the pterygoid wing in Aplestosuchus.
facts.quote: Una única fosa paracoanal rostrolateral que va a la fenestra paracoanal se encuentra en la base del ala del pterigoideo.

facts.statement: In Aplestosuchus, external jaw sculpture is limited to the dentary, and the occipital surface of the mandibular symphysis lacks a peg.
facts.quote: En la mandíbula de Aplestosuchus, la escultura externa de la mandíbula se limita al dentario, y la superficie occipital de la sínfisis mandibular carece de clavija.

facts.statement: Additionally, the crested border of the angular bone does not cover the rostral border of the mandibular fenestra, and a row of foramina exists between the mandibular fenestra and the ectopterygoid-yugal suture.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, el borde crestado del hueso angular no cubre el borde rostral de la fenestra mandibular, y hay una fila de forámenese entre la fenestra mandibular y la sutura del ectopterygoide y el yugal.

facts.statement: Non-autapomorphic traits such as the quadrate depression, medial approach of prefrontals, and the ectopterygoid-yugal articulation border confirm the classification of A. sordidus within Baurusuchidae.
facts.quote: Algunos de los rasgos no autapomórficos de A. sordidus listados anteriormente, como la depresión del cuadrado, la aproximación medial de los prefrontales, y el borde en la articulación ectopterygoide-yugal, confirman su clasificación dentro de Baurusuchidae.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Aplestosuchus is Baurusuchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Baurusuchinae

facts.statement: Aplestosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Aplestosuchus is Aplestosuchus sordidus.
facts.quote: Type species: Aplestosuchus sordidus

facts.statement: Aplestosuchus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The specimen was preserved lying on its side, in the same death posture as other baurusuchids collected from the site.
facts.quote: Fue preservado yaciendo sobre un lado, en la misma postura de muerte de otros baurusúquidos recolectados en el sitio.
